venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Baugh ran it like he built the thing. Everyone else played off that.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — fine-line rewrite for Charles. Fan rail stays empty.
headline: Baugh ran this offense. He went north when the hole was there, he bounced outside when it closed, and he left the field when they came down to stop him. Philo got the ball out of his hand. The receivers and tight ends blocked. That is Florida on this tape.

offense.body:
Baugh is the problem on this tape. He does not wait for a hole to open twice. If the line moves somebody, he is already through it, north, pad down. If that first hole closes, he plants and goes outside — that bounce is why a stuffed run still becomes 18. If the safety steps down into the box to help on him, there is nobody left over the top and he is gone. That is 160 yards. It does not look like they are asking him to invent a run. It looks like he already knows what the play is supposed to be.

The line is why that run stays a run. Harris is the left guard. Lovett, Moore, Shanahan, and Ugorji are the rest of the first five. Watch the first man who shows up in the hole. Somebody in orange is still on him. Baugh is already past that spot. That is blocking that lasts longer than the first hit. When the crease dies, the edge is still there for the bounce. That is the same five, just a different place they won.

They did not run it one way. Some plays are straight downhill, between the tackles, everybody coming north. Some plays start the same and then the line and Baugh take it wide, so FAU has to chase. What you almost never see is Philo dropping straight back and waiting while Baugh sits next to him as the outlet. He is in the shotgun. He sees the look. He throws it. He is on to the next one. Wilson, Stockton, Harpring, Clark coming out of the backfield — whoever the defense gives him, the ball is gone before the second wave can get there. That is a quarterback operating, not hunting. The one time he holds it, Sweeney is sitting in the window and the half ends with the ball in the other color.

Brown is who he is after he catches it. The long touchdown is not a deep ball they sat on all week. Philo throws it on time, short, because the corner is playing off so nothing goes over his head. First man misses. Then Brown is a problem in space. He does it again later with a little more air on the throw. Explosive. After the catch. That is the tape on him.

Clark runs. When Baugh is off the field, Clark is downhill, through the first man, and he has a long one of his own around the end. The touchdown where he slips out of the backfield is the same run look. The linebackers stay in to stop the give. Nobody goes with Clark. He catches it at the 4 and drives it in. He is a runner who can do that. He is not a change-of-pace they hid.

The wideouts and tight ends are in the run. They are not standing and watching. You see it when Baugh bounces and somebody in orange is still on the edge. You see it when Stockton finishes a short throw and gets north. Abrams’ long ball is what happens when FAU finally puts extra bodies in the box to stop Baugh. Faulkner does not live on that throw. He takes it when they come down.

They survive their own mess because the back is still the play. A bad snap loses a chunk inside the five. Baugh gets them back to the doorstep. Philo walks it in himself. That is not a gadget night. That is a team that kept giving it to the right guy.
bullets: Baugh is the problem — north when it is there, outside when it dies, gone when they come down.
The line stays on the first man long enough for that run to be real.
Philo gets it out. The Sweeney ball is the one he holds.
Brown after the catch. Clark runs. The skill guys block.

defense.body:
This defense comes downhill. They send four after the quarterback and they drop everyone else. They put another defensive back on the receiver who lines up inside, so the easy throw in the middle is not easy. The corners play off — a few yards of cushion — so nothing goes over their heads. Graham and Chiles are coming with the rush and they are in the run. The front is moving people, not sitting and reading.

James is on this tape. He drops a back for a loss. He gets Veltkamp on the ground. He hurries him. He is the tackle that ends a half. Lyons is on this tape. He and Flowers drop a catch for a loss. He and Graham share a sack. That is the line you saw, not a name from the depth chart.

They will give you yards underneath. Short. Outside. First down. That is the trade if the corners are going to stay deep. What they do with the next throw is go get it. When Veltkamp holds the ball, Coleman is already in the window. Johnson goes up and takes the other one. Coleman is on that breakup too. They run to the ball. When they tackle, the play is over.

The points they gave are jobs they did not finish. They packed the goal line — every body in a phone booth — and still lost the yard. They sent four and the end left the edge, so Veltkamp kept it and walked in. They played off and lost the ball in the back corner when Valsin stacked Flowers and won the fade. Same defense. Three jobs.

Bett finishes the last one. Veltkamp keeps it again. Bett gets there. The ball comes out. Myles Johnson is on it. That is the rush winning the one fight they had been playing for all night.

Campbell will throw the short one and run the quarterback. Tackle the first. The end has to stay outside on the second.
bullets: Four rush. Corners off. Another defensive back on the inside receiver.
James and Lyons show up — losses, a sack, a hurry.
They give the short throw. They take the one he holds.
The points are the pile, the quarterback run, and the fade.

specials.body: The drive stalled and they took the points. Durkin made it from 53. Florida never punted. They did not give the ball back on fourth down.
bullets: Durkin from 53. They took the points.

nextWeek.look: They will go fast and throw it short. Baugh is still the problem. White will still send four. Tackle the short one. The end stays outside on the quarterback run.
